comparisons.D10: For me it saved the handover step: the extracts I had already checked were gathered into a record I could pass on, instead of being copied out again.
comparisons.D2: My preference was the Prototype. I could see the claim, its source and what I was about to do on the same screen. I still opened the transcript, but I was not constantly moving between sheets.
comparisons.D7: I would need the links to land on the right passage every time, and it must stay obvious that the researcher—not the system—makes the final call. I would also want a clear edit trail.
comparisons.D8: If I could not get back to the participant's own words, I would not trust it. The same applies if uncertain material starts looking like a finished finding.
comparisons.D9: Fix the ordering. The topic groups make sense, but the E numbers should not jump around the page.
comparisons.name: P01

comparisons.D10: The approval constraint was the principal benefit: an unresolved attribution issue became visible before the statement entered the reviewed dataset.
comparisons.D2: I favoured the Prototype because incomplete verification remained explicit and prevented closure. Under the spreadsheet condition, reaching the same judgement relied on coordinating several fields distributed across worksheets.
comparisons.D7: Use in research would require stable references, access to the whole transcript and an intelligible provenance record. Validation should additionally cover messier interview material rather than only controlled examples.
comparisons.D8: I would discontinue use if lexical similarity began to stand in for evidential support, or if the design made the wider conversational context less accessible.
comparisons.D9: Present the quotation alongside the proposition under review. A failed test should identify the nature of the discrepancy, rather than returning a generic result.
comparisons.name: P02

comparisons.D10: Primary value was the controlled gate before release. The decisive artefact was the correction trail explaining the final treatment of E3 through E6.
comparisons.D2: Prototype. It worked as a pre-sign-off control, with one inspection path from assertion to anchor to disposition. The E4/E5 corrections also revealed where operator vigilance is still required.
comparisons.D7: Entry conditions: sample-check source anchors; lock revision history; assign different states to unsupported content and unanswered requirements.
comparisons.D8: Stop criterion: approval conceals a prior correction, or topical relevance is allowed to pass as substantiation.
comparisons.D9: Create two separate failure labels—'unsupported assertion' and 'coverage gap'—then display the quoted source at the decision point.
